prompt:
A student in a physics laboratory must select measuring instruments for three tasks:
Task 1: Measuring the diameter of a thin nylon monofilament (expected diameter ~ 0.25 mm).
Task 2: Measuring the internal diameter of a 50 cm^3 glass beaker (expected diameter ~ 45 mm).
Task 3: Measuring the length of a copper wire suspended from the ceiling (length ~ 2.4 m).
For each task, name the most suitable instrument from: metre rule, vernier calipers, micrometer screw gauge. Justify each choice by comparing the required measurement with the instrument resolution and geometry. [3]

mark_scheme.criterion: Task 1: Micrometer screw gauge; its resolution (0.01 mm) is much smaller than the 0.25 mm diameter, allowing reliable measurement.
Task 2: Vernier calipers; its internal jaws fit inside the beaker and its resolution (0.1 mm) is suitable for a 45 mm dimension.
Task 3: Metre rule (or 3 m tape measure); the dimension is large (~2.4 m) so a 1 mm resolution produces a negligible fractional uncertainty (~0.04%).

hints: Match the size of each object to an instrument whose resolution is suitably fine.
Check whether internal or external jaws are required.
solution: Task 1: Micrometer screw gauge (0.01 mm resolution is suited for 0.25 mm). Task 2: Vernier calipers (internal jaws and 0.1 mm resolution). Task 3: Metre rule / tape measure (1 mm resolution is sufficient for 2.4 m).
teacher_walkthrough: Task 1: 0.25 mm is small; 0.01 mm resolution from a micrometer gives ~4% resolution limit.
Task 2: internal diameter requires internal jaws found on vernier calipers; 0.1 mm gives ~0.2% resolution limit.
Task 3: 2.4 m requires a metre rule or tape; 1 mm gives 1 / 2400 = 0.04% resolution limit.

provenance.independence_statement: Authored 3-part apparatus selection matching instruments to dimensions and resolution.
